definition: California Assembly Bill 2013 (AB 2013) is a California law requiring developers of generative artificial intelligence systems to publicly disclose information about the data used to train their models.
details: The law passed unanimously in both the Senate and the Assembly, and took effect on January 1, 2026.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. That next-word, next-stroke magic is California Assembly Bill 2013 (2024).
